summary: Notion splits the world in two: internal integrations, which work instantly for your own workspace, and public integrations, which any workspace can install through OAuth. Public ones go through a security review before Notion publishes them.

rationale: Internal use has zero friction - no review at all.
Public integrations need Notion's security review before publication.
The capability model (read/insert/update checkboxes) is simpler than classic scope lists.

timeEstimate.setup: About 30 minutes to create a public integration and run OAuth against a test workspace.
timeEstimate.approval: Roughly a few days to a week for the security review, based on Notion's review documentation; not a published SLA.

basis.text: Notion documents a security review for public integrations.
Exact review duration is not guaranteed anywhere - treat it as an estimate.

steps.title: Create the integration
steps.detail: In Notion, go to Settings > Connections > Develop or manage integrations (or notion.so/profile/integrations) and create a new integration. Choose Public if other workspaces will install it.

steps.title: Fill in the public listing basics
steps.detail: Public integrations need a company name, a privacy policy URL, a terms URL and a support contact before Notion lets you submit.

steps.title: Configure OAuth and capabilities
steps.detail: Add your redirect URI and tick only the capabilities you need (read content, insert content, etc.).

steps.title: Test, then submit for review
steps.detail: Install it into a test workspace through the OAuth URL. When it behaves, submit - Notion's team reviews security practices before publishing.

requirements.item: A Notion account and a workspace to develop in
Privacy policy URL, terms URL and support contact (public integrations)

gotchas.text: An integration only sees pages explicitly shared with it - most 'API returns nothing' bugs are unshared pages, not auth problems.
Capabilities are broad checkboxes, not fine-grained scopes; you can't request half of one.

agentCanDo: Re-read Notion's authorization and security-review docs and refresh this guide
Check whether your planned API calls fit the capability checkboxes
developerMustDo: Create the integration under their own Notion account
Write and host the privacy policy and terms pages
Submit for the security review and answer questions
